# Ādiccupaṭṭhānajātaka (Ja 175)

**ID:** Ja 175
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Ādiccupaṭṭhānajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Monkey Who Worshiped the Sun
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja175

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ādiccupaṭṭhānajātaka* (Ja 175) is a canonical birth story found in the Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. As recorded in the canonical-commentarial framing, the story was told by the Buddha while residing at Jetavana regarding a rogue or hypocritical monk (*kuhaka*), with the opening verse beginning *Sabbesu kira bhūtesu* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. In the past story set during the reign of Brahmadatta in Bārāṇasī, the Bodhisatta was born into a brahmin family in Kāsi, studied at Takkasilā, and went forth as an ascetic leader (*gaṇasatthā*) [Fausböll 1879]. The narrative centers on a mischievous monkey who hypocritically mimics religious devotions by posturing as if venerating the sun [Revire 2016; Fausböll 1879]. In the *samodhāna*, the Buddha reveals that the deceitful monkey was reborn as the rogue monk, the ascetic disciples were the Buddhist community, and the ascetic master was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1879].

Scholars note that the text functions as Buddhist satire directed against contemporary solar cults and ritual sun-worship (*ādiccupaṭṭhāna*), a practice condemned as wrong livelihood in the *Brahmajālasutta* of the *Dīgha Nikāya* and subjected to mockery in this Jātaka [Dayal 1932; Revire 2016]. 

SuttaCentral records four modern translations across four languages, but lists no curated cross-corpus parallels [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies Pali-internal text reuse exclusively within the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo), comprising five matching passages (311 characters) centered on the story and verses [DharmaNexus].
